## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Apaṇṇakajātaka* (Ja 1) is the opening text of the canonical Pali *Jātaka* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya, which traditionally commences a corpus of 550 birth stories [Appleton 2010; Norman 1983]. According to the frame narrative, the discourse concerning truth was delivered by the Buddha while residing at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī. In the narrative of the past, the Bodhisatta is depicted as a wise caravan leader [Appleton 2010]. The prose commentary includes an exegesis on the word *kantāra* ("wilderness") [Norman 1983], and the narrative includes the standard "story of the present" (*paccuppannavatthu*) [Appleton 2010].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Paṭhamo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a1) (§2.1–3.1 ↔ §900–902_0)
- [Appleton 2010] Naomi Appleton, Jātaka Stories in Theravāda Buddhism: Narrating the Bodhisatta Path (2010) — Narrative role of the Bodhisatta as caravan leader, presence of paccuppannavatthu, and earlier parallel in Dīgha Nikāya Pāyāsi Sutta.
- [Norman 1983] K. R. Norman, Pali Literature: Including the Canonical Literature in Prakrit and Sanskrit of all the Hīnayāna Schools of Buddhism (1983) — Position of Apaṇṇaka at the start of the 550 Jātakas and commentarial exegesis on kantāra.
